title: Adaptive chunk orchestration for KV-resident fragments and GPU compaction policy
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: As token sequence distributions and continuous-batching patterns vary, the KV cache experiences high internal fragmentation despite aggressive eviction policies. On multi-tenant GPUs fragmentation increases tail memory usage and forces spurts of full-cache compaction that spike latency. Current allocator heuristics operate at coarse slab sizes and do not align allocation boundaries to typical KV-value footprints or batch token length distributions. Goal: Introduce an allocation orchestration layer that allocates KV entries as variable-sized 'chunks' grouped into micro-regions, enabling in-place micro-coalescing, bounded background compaction, and allocation steering tied to continuous-batching signals to reduce fragmentation and smooth GPU memory usage.
proposal: 1) Chunk abstraction: allocate KV values in 256B-aligned chunks with an optional small-header for metadata. Chunks pack into micro-regions (configurable: 4KB, 16KB, 64KB) to allow intra-region compaction without global surgery. 2) Live migration policy: when region fragmentation exceeds a threshold, schedule bounded live-copy of hot entries into a new compacted region using a GPU memcpy kernel with preemptible checkpoints; use copy-on-write to keep reads consistent. 3) Allocation steering: integrate with continuous-batching controller to bias new allocations into hot regions when request latency profile indicates frequent short-prefix reuse. 4) Eviction hints: augment LRU with frequency and contiguous-span scoring so small contiguous spans of chunks have higher coalescing priority. 5) Background compaction epochs: run rate-limited compaction kernels during low utilization windows; provide CPU-side fallback for constrained GPUs. 6) GPU arena manager: maintain per-stream arenas to avoid cross-stream fragmentation and allow bulk release of drained regions. 7) Minimal metadata: store compact region directory on host pinned memory; avoid per-chunk heavy metadata on device. 8) Telemetry hooks: emit region-level fragmentation ratio, compaction time, and allocation steering hits for dashboards and automated rollback triggers.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (spike): microbench on single-GPU with synthetic trace (3d). Phase 1 (canary): enable on a small percentage of production traffic pinned to non-critical tenants with compaction disabled but allocation steering on (2w). Phase 2: enable bounded background compaction and live-copy with strict CPU/GPU time budgets (2w). Phase 3: monitor 2 weeks, tune thresholds, widen rollout. Rollback knob: disable allocation steering and drain arenas; disable compaction kernels. Manual escalation path in runbook.
acceptance_criteria: 10-20% reduction in device tail memory under representative continuous-batching traces
No more than 5% P90 latency regression on gen requests during background compaction windows
Compaction jobs do not exceed configured GPU time budget (default 50ms per epoch)
Telemetry shows region fragmentation ratio improvement of >=40% in canary tenancy
Automated rollback successfully drains and restores previous allocator within 30 minutes

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Compaction jobs could interfere with hot inference traffic -> Mitigation: strict GPU time budgets and priority demotion; pause compaction when P95 latency > SLO
Risk: Copy-on-write could increase peak memory usage temporarily -> Mitigation: budget for transient peak and throttle compaction granularity; prefer moving cold entries first
Risk: Metadata syncing bug could cause stale pointers -> Mitigation: memory-safe epoch markers and verification checksums during canary
Risk: Increased CPU overhead for steering decisions -> Mitigation: approximate heuristics and batch decisions per controller tick
